content.comment_body: Hello all! I'm attempting to update the firmware of a [product_name] device from [version_no] to [version_no], but when I insert the SD card, the device starts up normally and begins rebooting repeatedly without completing the upgrade. Has anyone encountered this before? I've attached a screenshot showing the SD card's root content—it's formatted in FAT32. Thank you in advance for any suggestions.

It appears that the SD card may not be formatted in FAT32. Additionally, [product_name] version [version_no] supports exFAT, so formatting it as FAT32 isn't mandatory. You can check the SD card's status in the system menu under diagnostics.

If that's the message, then the [product_name] isn't detecting the SD card. Consider trying a different SD card.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing firmware upgrade challenges on [product_name] devices when using SD cards. Even after following recommended formatting procedures and testing with multiple SD cards and hardware units, the device fails to detect the card, making it impossible to perform the update. The lack of explicit error messages leaves uncertainty about whether the issue lies in the SD card, formatting method, or the device itself.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a simple and dependable firmware update using officially supported SD cards and formats, along with clear device feedback to diagnose any problems.
